text: The Lookup activity retrieves a dataset, or even just a single value, from any source Data Factory supports — so a later activity can use it dynamically instead of relying on a hard-coded value baked into the pipeline itself. Configure a source dataset, exactly like a Copy activity's source, except nothing actually gets copied anywhere at all.

One single setting fundamentally changes the shape of what comes back. firstRowOnly true, the default, returns a single row under a fixed firstRow key. Set it to false instead, and you get every matching row back as a value array, with a count of how many — exactly the shape a ForEach activity, in Chapter 4, expects to iterate over directly.

Real limits worth knowing before you rely on this: a maximum of five thousand rows returned, a maximum of four megabytes of total output, and a query or stored procedure used for a lookup must return exactly one result set, or the activity fails outright.

The Stored Procedure activity invokes a real stored procedure in Azure SQL Database, Azure Synapse Analytics, or SQL Server. Pick a linked service, pick the procedure, supply its parameters — the natural choice for logic that already genuinely lives inside the database itself, like logging a pipeline run's completion.

One real limitation worth remembering: the Stored Procedure activity doesn't support output parameters at all. A procedure that actually needs to return a value back to the pipeline needs the Lookup activity instead — Stored Procedure is strictly a one-way call. Next: Web, Wait, Fail, and Set Variable — four smaller activities that round out nearly every pipeline's toolkit.
